learningObjectives: Differentiate working, episodic, semantic and procedural memory.
Explain hippocampal binding and systems consolidation.
Distinguish encoding, storage and retrieval failures.
Apply memory-system distinctions to clinical assessment.

anatomy.label: Frontoparietal working memory
anatomy.detail: Distributed frontal and parietal systems sustain task-relevant representations.
anatomy.clinical: ADHD, fatigue and anxiety may reduce effective capacity through attentional competition.

anatomy.label: Hippocampal formation
anatomy.detail: Hippocampal circuits link people, places, time and context into retrievable episodes.
anatomy.clinical: Bilateral damage causes profound anterograde episodic-memory impairment.

anatomy.label: Distributed semantic cortex
anatomy.detail: Temporal and association cortices encode conceptual features across modalities.
anatomy.clinical: Anterior temporal degeneration can produce progressive loss of word and object meaning.

anatomy.label: Striatum and cerebellum
anatomy.detail: Repeated action-outcome patterns become efficient through corticostriatal and cerebellar learning.
anatomy.clinical: Procedural learning may remain relatively intact despite severe episodic amnesia.

anatomy.label: Prefrontal retrieval control
anatomy.detail: Prefrontal systems organise cues and evaluate whether retrieved information fits current goals.
anatomy.clinical: Executive dysfunction can mimic amnesia through disorganised retrieval.

interaction.title: Explore the Memory Systems
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Attend
stages.text: Selective attention determines what information receives effective processing.

stages.label: Encode
stages.text: Features are organised and bound into a usable representation.

stages.label: Consolidate
stages.text: Synaptic and systems processes stabilise memory across time.

stages.label: Monitor
stages.text: Executive systems evaluate confidence, source and accuracy.

quizBank.question: The hippocampus is especially important for:
quizBank.explanation: The hippocampal formation links distributed features into context-rich episodic representations.

quizBank.question: Which memory system supports learned skills and habits?
quizBank.explanation: Procedural learning relies strongly on corticostriatal and cerebellar circuits.

quizBank.question: Poor attention during learning most directly impairs:
quizBank.explanation: Information that is not effectively attended to is less likely to be encoded for later retrieval.

quizBank.question: Working memory relies heavily on:
quizBank.explanation: Distributed prefrontal and parietal systems maintain and manipulate task-relevant information.

quizBank.question: A retrieval failure differs from storage loss because:
options: The representation may remain available but inaccessible with current cues
quizBank.explanation: Retrieval can fail despite retained information, particularly when cueing or executive search is weak.

prompts: Name the major components of the Memory Systems.
Explain one clinically relevant function of the Memory Systems.
Identify one common oversimplification to avoid.
